forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred over NSW will extend a ridge westwards over SA during Friday and Saturday. A cold front will approach from the west late Saturday then move across SA on Sunday. Another high pressure system will move eastwards across waters to the south during Monday then over Victoria on Tuesday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.
Dry and mostly sunny. Maximum temperatures above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds freshening in the far west during the afternoon and about coastal areas overnight.
Dry and mostly clear evening. Northeast to northwesterly winds, tending east to southeasterly in the far northeast.

Isolated light showers about the southern agricultural area during the afternoon and evening. Chance of an isolated thunderstorm in the far northwest later. Maximum temperatures above average. North to northwesterly winds becoming fresh and gusty ahead of a southwesterly change extending across the west and south, tending southwest to southeasterly during the evening.

text.p: Chance of an isolated light morning shower about the southern agricultural areas and a possible isolated thunderstorm in the far northwest later. Maximum temperatures below average in the south but above average in the north. South to southeasterly winds, fresh in the northeast during the afternoon.

Cold at first with patchy frost about the agricultural area. Dry apart from the chance of a shower in the far southwest during the late afternoon and evening. Maximum temperatures above average. Northeasterly winds, but fresh southeasterly in the far northeast. Afternoon sea breezes near the coast.
Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: less than 1 to 2 mm about the southern agricultural area and in the far northwest.
